primary_metric: ss-eval --split test PSNR of the PBR rendering vs paper supp. Table 360psnr (garden 25.72, counter 26.22); compare the drop vs our gsplat baseline (baseline3dgs-mipnerf360-30000: garden 26.89, counter 28.85) with the paper's drop vs 3DGS (garden -1.69, counter -2.48)
baseline: baseline3dgs-mipnerf360-30000 (same images_4 / images_2 folders, -r 1 = official GS-IR resolution protocol); no new baseline run needed
notes: --steps 40000 is required (30000 initial stage + baking + 10000 decomposition; stage switch hard-coded at pbr_start 30000). Default bench.py args (--recipe 3dgs --num-gaussians 10000000) are correct. Baking at step 30000 runs inside ss-train (garden ~480k probes, counter ~216k; ~5-20 min depending on GPU load). First use JIT-compiles ss_gsir/csrc/gsir_kernels.cu (~1 min, cached). ss-eval restores the GS-IR bank from <run>/checkpoint.pt via its --run argument (works with bench.py's ss-eval call unchanged). Official LPIPS fed [0,1] images; runtime uses [-1,1] (LPIPS not directly comparable).
